text: Practitioner reading of 5.1.2(i): the consent screen must name the provider (not 'powered by AI'), say what the AI does, list concrete data types, require an affirmative tap, appear before the first API call, and be revocable from Settings. This is community interpretation, not Apple text. (medium confidence)

text: Guideline 2.3.1(a) says new features, functionality and product changes must be described with specificity in Notes for Review (generic descriptions will be rejected) and be accessible for review; hidden or dormant features are prohibited. An optional key-gated AI feature counts. (high confidence)

text: Guideline 2.1(a) requires demo account info if the app includes a login, and allows a built-in demo mode only with prior Apple approval. A BYOK feature has no Apple-provisioned account, so the notes should either supply a reviewer-only key/endpoint with quota or state the feature is optional, off by default, and not required to use the app, ideally with a screen recording. (medium confidence)
keywords: BYO API key consent design and Notes for Review template for optional AI and alert features

text: Notes for Review template shape: keep to a few lines; state where the feature lives (menu path), default state, what data is sent to which named provider, how consent is revoked, that core features work without it, and credentials/demo path tested on a fresh install. Direct instructions beat marketing copy. (medium confidence)
keywords: BYO API key consent design and Notes for Review template for optional AI and alert features

text: Guideline 2.4.5(vi) bars Mac App Store apps from presenting a license screen at launch or requiring license keys. Putting the BYO API key prompt behind an optional Settings pane, never at launch, keeps it away from this rule; the guideline does not mention API keys for third-party services. (medium confidence)
